newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims

R-Revised, March 29 Initial Claims from 314,000, March 22 from 313,000, March 29 4-Week Average from 312,500, March 22 from 312,000, March 22 Continued Claims from 2,300,000, and March 15 from 2,310,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 313,000 in the April 5 week.
Labor said nine states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended March 29, the latest period for which data are available.

They were Maryland, with 2,774 fewer claims filings; Louisiana, with 2,657; North Carolina, with 2,583; Texas, with 1,990; California, with 1,895; Kentucky, with 1,780; Michigan, with 1,753; Illinois, with 1,395; and Tennessee, with 1,361.
Maryland had fewer layoffs in the automobile and service industries. Louisiana had fewer layoffs in transportation equipment, and North Carolina had fewer layoffs in the textile industry.

Texas reported fewer layoffs in electrical equipment and trade industries. Illinois had fewer layoffs in trade, service and manufacturing industries, while Michigan had fewer layoffs in various industries throughout the state. Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in the apparel, lumber, printing and publishing, transportation equipment and service industries.
California and Kentucky had no comment.

Georgia, with 1,553 additional filings, was the only states reporting an increase in claims exceeding 1,000 in the March 29 week. The state cited more layoffs in the automobile and transportation equipment industries.
